I6's major was a FALSE POSITIVE caused by invariants.running_arm(), which inferred the in-flight arm from the most recent arm_*.log. Those files are never deleted, so it answered 'confirm__null_floor' long after that arm exited at 15:47:50, I6 called a correctly-ordered search out of order, and the arbiter escalated to WRONG and halted. No data was lost: confirm__null_floor's record IS present (verdict not_confirmed, contamination clean, 0.5080 vs 0.4645 = +0.0435) -- it landed after the contamination check, which takes minutes. running_arm() now asks the PROCESS whether anything is in flight and uses the log only to name it; a negative control was added. I6 now reports 'idle; next up would be null1'.

I10 was RIGHT and the underlying state was wrong, not the invariant. confirm__null_floor failed its fresh-seed confirmation (+0.0435 on seed 9001 against the +0.0665 it was selected on -- seed luck, not an effect, which is exactly what the confirmation discipline exists to catch) and left a 1.7 GB checkpoint whose artifact field was BLANK. A blank field is indistinguishable from a verification that silently did not run, the same 'absent rather than red' shape as the contamination field I9 caught earlier. Two fixes: the daemon now writes an explicit artifact value for every checkpointed arm, and I10 distinguishes a KEPT arm (critical -- that model is the deliverable) from a NON-KEPT arm's checkpoint (evidence, marked as such, not a critical). Existing record backfilled. 12/12 invariants now hold. The 1.7 GB of failed-confirmation weights is a separate decision I have not made.

each finding read and closed with evidence, not waived. integrity/I13: discarded weights collected (1.79 GB, null1) via pipeline/lineage.py --apply; weights are lineage, the number is the record. adversary/A4: the recorded bar no longer followed any rule. The rule itself was wrong, not just the number: it took twice the LARGEST observed null, and these null arms are replicas of a recipe that TRAINS, so their deltas are the training effect (+0.068), not noise. That set the bar at +0.188, above every effect upstream reports, reproducing upstream's own diagnosed failure (a threshold above the design's resolution) in a new disguise. The bar is now one rule, do_nothing_mean + resolvable increment, derived at the seed budget a decisive arm actually runs; state/power.json was regenerated by the production path, and A4 now re-derives it to the same number. The old rule stood at +0.0450 while doing nothing was worth +0.0680, which is why the first null arm was recorded kept_pending_confirm. provenance/I2: null2 is re-running at the seed its prediction names (37); the 10:17 run that left records/null2 behind was one of the three duplicate runs D1 already discarded, at seed 17, and it is quarantined under versions/quarantine/. New gates: run_one.py refuses a spec whose seed is not the preregistered one, and the prereg now pins the seed. Tests in tests/test_gates.py cover all of it, including a duplicate-run detector over records/.

C2 is true and self-inflicted: power.py and loop.py were corrected on disk at 18:45 while the daemon that started at 18:44 held the old modules in memory, which is exactly the quiet divergence C2 exists to catch. The arm in flight was 4 minutes into a 60-minute run and its record would have been written by the stale process, so it is discarded and re-run rather than kept. Restarting under launchd, which owns the lifecycle, instead of by hand -- a hand-started daemon plus the next StartInterval tick is how two null2 processes came to run at once at 18:44.
